correctness.rationale: For all odd N>=5: circulant Fourier diagonalization gives multiplier. Explicit geometric sums yield F(0)=-1, F(1)<0, F(2)>0. Coefficient sequence has one sign change at N=5,7 and two at N>=9; exponential Descartes plus the opposite signs at s->-infinity, 0 and 2 prove a single simple positive root in (1,2). Uniform second-derivative bound O(N^2 log^2 N) and Riemann convergence of F prime(1)/N^2 prove the inverse-square transition and exact cosine-integral constant. Positive Fourier eigenvalue directly violates conditional negative type; -F derivative of kernel at t=0 gives sharp small-t failure. Portable checker verifies explicit finite examples, not the all-order claim.

value.rationale: The first even nontrivial cyclic Fourier sector yields a natural finite-graph negative-type obstruction. The result resolves its unique root for every odd order, establishes the first sharp inverse-square approach to one with a cosine-integral coefficient, and gives explicit necessary failure of Gaussian graph-distance kernels. This quantitatively complements the known strict 1-negative-type gap; it does not rely on claiming the full supremal exponent.
